Why go: your own driver, without the taxi haggling

Koh Samui's taxis rarely use the meter and prices for a day of sightseeing vary wildly. A private van with a driver at a fixed price is the easiest way for families and groups to see the island at their own pace, and the only comfortable option for 6–10 people travelling together. The same vans also run long-distance transfers to Phuket and Bangkok for groups who would rather not split up across flights.

What you'll do

You decide. A 4-hour booking covers the north-east highlights such as the Big Buddha, Wat Plai Laem and Fisherman's Village. Six to eight hours is enough for a full loop of the ring road with Na Muang waterfall, the Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks and a west-coast sunset. Ten hours suits a long day with lunch, shopping and dinner.

Who it suits

  • Families with young children and car seats, and groups of 5–10.
  • Visitors who don't want to ride a scooter on Samui's busy roads.
  • Groups moving on to Phuket or Bangkok with lots of luggage.

Who should choose something else

  • Couples on a budget: a shared half-day highlights tour costs less.
  • Travellers going to Bangkok: a flight is much faster. See Bangkok to Koh Samui for the options.

Good to know

  • Child seats: not standard in Thai vans; ask us in advance.
  • Timing: extra hours cost 500 THB each, agreed with the driver on the day.
  • Long trips: ferry timetables and weather can delay mainland transfers, especially from October to December.

Before you book

Choose the number of hours and send us a rough list of stops, your pickup point and the number of passengers and suitcases. For Phuket or Bangkok, tell us your flight or check-in time so we can plan the ferry crossing with enough margin.
